speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your newborn check-up. I will ask you a few questions about your baby's health to ensure they are developing correctly. Do you know if your baby has had any feeding difficulties, color changes, or unusual movements since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing those details. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunizations, has the infant received any shots yet, and have you noticed any yellowing of the skin or eyes since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome) with associated congenital heart defect (likely truncus arteriosus or Tetralogy of Fallot), congenital cataracts, and sensorineural hearing loss.

The combination of a continuous heart murmur, bluish non-blanching skin macules (likely port-wine stains or vascular anomalies), bilateral cataracts, and hearing loss is highly suggestive of a complex congenital syndrome, potentially involving 22q11.2 deletion or a chromosomal rearrangement. I request a FISH test for 22q11.2 deletion and a chromosomal microarray analysis.
